title.en: Practical 1: Diameter of a spherical body (Vernier caliper)

text.en: How do you measure a cricket ball more exactly than a ruler can?

The aim is to find the diameter of a spherical body, such as a cricket ball, using a Vernier caliper. The apparatus needed is the Vernier caliper and the ball.
First find the least count: one main scale division is 1 mm and one Vernier division is 0.9 mm, so the least count is 0.1 mm or 0.01 cm in the book's scale. Find the zero correction, fix the ball between the lower jaws, note the main scale reading (MSR) and the Vernier coincidence (VC), and repeat at different positions of the ball.
Diameter = MSR + (VC x LC) with the zero correction added or subtracted. Record at least three readings in a table, find the average and write the result as the diameter in cm.
